answer: A Sybil cluster’s marginal attack cost scales super-linearly because each additional identity demands a trellis of bonded collateral, while quadratic slashing erodes the entire ledge’s stake at an accelerating rate, making the k-th node’s expected loss proportional to k²; thus, extracting nectar from protocol value V requires expending C·k², which exceeds V when k exceeds √(V/C), a threshold that collateralized capital lockup enforces deterministically.
